subject: Re: EU→US data transfer - DLP & TIA controls for GutFirm Health
messages:
From: Julia Kramer <jkramer@gutfirm.com>

Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@gutfirm.com>, GutFirm Privacy Team <privacy@gutfirm.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU→US data transfer - DLP & TIA questionnaire

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — we liked the latency and rollout controls. Our privacy team is working on the Transfer Impact Assessment for the upcoming deployment of GutFirm Health's patient-messaging feature. To complete the TIA we need a set of technical controls and evidence about cross-border handling.

Key items we need:
- Confirmation of where customer data may be processed (regions/zones).
- Whether Redwood acts as controller or processor for logs/metadata.
- Confirmed use of SCCs (and which addendum) and whether you support DPAs with SCCs attached.
- DLP controls for PHI/PII: in-flight scanning, masking, retention enforcement.
- Encryption at rest (keys KMS/HSM) and in transit.
- Subprocessor list and recent SOC 2 report (redacted OK).
- Any DPIA you maintain for similar deployments.

I attached our TIA questionnaire (GutFirm_TIA_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx). Can you let me know what you can share directly and what needs an NDA/DPA? If useful, we can set a 30-min call this week to walk through.

Appreciate the help — we are targeting a go/no-go decision by mid-December.

— Julia Kramer
Privacy Lead, GutFirm Health
[Attachment: GutFirm_TIA_Questionnaire_v3.xlsx]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Kramer <jkramer@gutfirm.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU→US data transfer - DLP & TIA questionnaire

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Looping in Hannah from Security and Vivek from Legal to make sure we provide the right artifacts and call out anything that requires a DPA/BAA.

Quick answers up front:
- Processing regions: hosted primarily in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 depending on routing; we can provide per-tenant exportability options on Redwood Private.
- Controller vs processor: Redwood is a processor for customer content; logs/operational telemetry are processed under our processing terms but we can scope logs on Dedicated/Private.
- SCCs/DPA: we have a DPA template with SCCs appended — legal can confirm.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest with customer-managed KMS available on Dedicated/Private.
- DLP: we have configurable PII/PHI redaction and automatic KV cache masking; will share a one-page DLP controls summary.

We can share SOC 2 (redacted) and our architecture diagram under NDA/DPA. Hannah — can you propose a minimal artifact set we can share now plus anything we should redact? Vivek — can you confirm whether BAA is required for this kind of deployment and next steps to get the DPA/Docusign link out?

Julia — happy to join a 30-min slot; propose Tue 12:00–12:30 UTC or Wed 09:00–09:30 UTC.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all — sharing the security/controls summary we typically provide for TIAs. I've attached two artifacts: a concise DLP controls PDF and a mapping matrix that aligns common TIA questions to our artifacts.

What we can share now (redacted where necessary):
- redwood_dlp_summary.pdf — covers detection rules, masking, and retention enforcement (no customer examples).
- redwood_tia_matrix.csv — maps GutFirm questionnaire rows to our artifacts and the required access level (public, NDA, DPA).
- SOC 2 report: available on request under NDA (we'll provide a redacted copy).
- Architecture diagram with data flow: available under DPA.

Notes on specific asks:
- SCCs/DPA: we use the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (2021 version) in our DPA.
- HIPAA/BAA: Redwood provides a Private deployment and contractual BAA for customers needing HIPAA protections; hosted customers can use dedicated capacity and contractual controls, but BAA requires review.
- Subprocessors: list will be provided as a CSV under DPA.

Julia — attaching the two artifacts now. If you can mark which rows of your questionnaire are must-have vs nice-to-have we can prioritize.

— Hannah
Director, Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben and Hannah — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our privacy team after reviewing the matrix:

1) SCCs: we will want the 2021 SCCs appended to a fully signed DPA. Can you confirm Redwood supports the 2021 SCCs in your standard DPA?
2) BAA/HIPAA: for our use-case the messages will contain PHI. If a hosted solution cannot meet a signed BAA, we will likely need a Private deployment or a BAA-enabled Dedicated arrangement.
3) DPIA: we typically include vendor DPIAs in our submission. Do you have a vendor DPIA or high-level risk assessment we can include?

We can share a prioritized list from our questionnaire today — sending that in a follow-up email. Can you also share a link to the DPA/DocuSign you mentioned and an ETA for SOC 2 under NDA?

— Tom
Senior Privacy Manager, GutFirm Health

- DPIA: we maintain a vendor DPIA summary for inference workloads; I'll attach the summary after DPA execution (we prefer to share the fuller PDF under DPA).
